tasks.prompt: Fix issue #1083 in xdist.scheduler.loadscope.LoadScopeScheduling.schedule. For one loadscope worker, preserve the collector's scope order even when loadscope reordering is enabled: sorting scopes cannot improve parallel balance when only one worker exists and it can violate required test-family order. Keep the existing largest-scope-first behavior for multiple workers and preserve --no-loadscope-reorder behavior.
acceptance: With one loadscope worker and loadscopereorder enabled, the first collected scope is sent before a later, larger scope.
With two workers and loadscopereorder enabled, the larger scope remains first for initial balancing.
With --no-loadscope-reorder semantics, two workers receive scopes in collection order and every collected item remains scheduled exactly once.
The production change is confined to src/xdist/scheduler/loadscope.py in LoadScopeScheduling.schedule.

tasks.prompt: Implement the explicitly benchmark-defined #1040 issue-family extension in xdist.scheduler.loadscope.LoadScopeScheduling.schedule. If config.option.loadscopecontroller exists, call it once for each collected nodeid while the controller builds loadscope work units. A truthy return means that callable ran the item on the controller, so do not enqueue it to any worker. A false return leaves normal scheduling untouched; absence of the optional callable preserves existing behavior. Do not claim this private callable is the public marker/CLI requested by #1040.
acceptance: An optional loadscopecontroller callable is invoked exactly once for every collected nodeid in collection order; a truthy return means it ran that nodeid on the controller and excludes it from worker batches.
Nodeids for which the callable returns false remain in their normal scope work unit without duplication or omission.
Without loadscopecontroller, loadscope scheduling retains its existing behavior.
This is explicitly an issue-family extension because LoadScopeScheduling has nodeids rather than pytest Item marker data.
The production change is confined to src/xdist/scheduler/loadscope.py in LoadScopeScheduling.schedule.

tasks.prompt: Fix pytest-xdist issue #1323 through LoadScopeScheduling._reschedule, the lifecycle hook inherited by LoadGroupScheduling. When a crashed loadgroup worker's workload is returned, discard completed work units before dispatching to its replacement. Never call send_runtest_some with an empty index list; preserve every incomplete grouped test for the replacement worker and let the scheduler finish normally.
acceptance: A restarted LoadGroupScheduling worker receives only the pending test index, never an empty send_runtest_some request for a completed group.
Completed work units returned from a crashed worker are discarded before dispatch while the pending grouped work unit remains scheduled.
The replacement can report the pending test complete, after which tests_finished is true and has_pending is false.
The production change is in src/xdist/scheduler/loadscope.py at LoadScopeScheduling._reschedule, inherited by LoadGroupScheduling.

tasks.prompt: Implement issue #1314 in the LoadScopeScheduling._reschedule lifecycle inherited by LoadGroupScheduling. Do not treat WorkerController.shutdown as immediate process termination: it appends a FIFO shutdown command and sets shutting_down before the worker consumes it. Retain the empty-workqueue shutdown calls, including initial-distribution shutdown after every runtests command has been enqueued; removing them deadlocks a worker waiting for its next command. Make tests_finished false while any assigned grouped test remains pending, even when that worker already has a queued graceful shutdown marker.
acceptance: After loadgroup dispatch exhausts the global queue, each assigned worker's runtests command precedes its queued shutdown marker, so every assigned grouped test remains runnable.
A queued graceful shutdown marker is not treated as premature termination and no post-final-report shutdown contract is required.
tests_finished remains false while either worker has a pending grouped test, then becomes true only after both assigned tests are reported complete.
The reference preserves the LoadScopeScheduling._reschedule shutdown path and updates its completion accounting without leaving pending work.

tasks.prompt: Fix open issue #1218 in xdist.plugin's --dist option parsing and pytest_cmdline_main. Track explicit --dist while parsing the option, rather than inspecting InvocationParams.args, so CLI, PYTEST_ADDOPTS, and ini addopts all preserve the configured distribution. Normalize an implicit default distribution mode to load for -n, but an explicitly supplied --dist value wins. In particular, retain --dist=worksteal with worker processes and let explicit --dist=no disable worker setup. Preserve -n0 as the disabling boundary. This benchmark-defined --dist=no case is an issue-family extension because the pinned base already preserves explicit non-no modes.
acceptance: With -n 2 and no explicit --dist, pytest_cmdline_main normalizes dist to load and creates two popen tx entries.
With --dist=worksteal and -n 2, it retains worksteal and creates two popen tx entries.
With explicit --dist=no and -n 2 from the CLI, PYTEST_ADDOPTS, or ini addopts, it retains no, clears worker count and tx, rather than silently selecting load.
With -n 0 and an explicit distributed mode, it disables distribution and clears tx.
Production changes are limited to src/xdist/plugin.py's pytest_addoption parser declaration and pytest_cmdline_main normalization.

tasks.prompt: Implement open enhancement #1221 in xdist.plugin.pytest_cmdline_main. Accept exactly -n auto-1, call the automatic-worker hook exactly once, reserve one worker by subtracting one without going below zero, and then reuse the existing distribution normalization. Treat auto-2 and malformed auto expressions as invalid, and preserve --pdb forcing the worker count to zero without auto detection.
acceptance: parse_numprocesses accepts auto-1 while rejecting auto-2, auto--1, and auto-one.
With an auto-worker hook result of 4, -n auto-1 becomes 3 workers, load distribution, and three popen tx entries.
With an auto-worker hook result of 1, -n auto-1 clamps at zero and disables distribution with no tx entries.
The automatic-worker hook is called exactly once for each non-pdb auto-1 resolution.
With --pdb, -n auto-1 disables workers without calling auto detection.
The production change is in src/xdist/plugin.py at xdist.plugin.pytest_cmdline_main.

tasks.prompt: Implement the benchmark-defined secondary load-group key extension in xdist.scheduler.loadscope.LoadScopeScheduling._split_scope. Issue #1008 requests a secondary distribution grouping for ungrouped loadgroup items, but does not specify an API or name loadscope. For this strict-overlap task, extend the existing xdist @group nodeid suffix convention: a top-level suffix after the final parametrization bracket is the scope key, while @ inside a parameter remains ordinary parameter text. Preserve normal loadscope grouping for untagged nodeids. This is an honest issue-family extension, not an upstream-specified public API.
acceptance: A nodeid ending in a top-level @group suffix returns that group name as its work-unit key.
A class test ending in a top-level @group suffix also returns the group name rather than its class scope.
An @ character inside a parametrization id is not interpreted as a secondary group key.
An untagged nodeid keeps the existing module-or-class loadscope key.
The production change is in src/xdist/scheduler/loadscope.py at xdist.scheduler.loadscope.LoadScopeScheduling._split_scope.

tasks.prompt: Fix issue #1335 in xdist.scheduler.loadscope.LoadScopeScheduling._split_scope. Derive the module-or-class scope before the first pytest parameter bracket, so :: inside a parameter id cannot become the rightmost separator. Preserve the existing unparametrized module, class, and doctest grouping behavior.
acceptance: A function parameter id containing cafe:cafe::cafe groups at its test module rather than splitting inside the parameter.
A class method parameter id containing :: groups at its class scope.
A doctest-style package __init__.py nodeid with an IPv6 parameter groups at the package path.
An unparametrized function retains its existing module scope.
The production change is in src/xdist/scheduler/loadscope.py at xdist.scheduler.loadscope.LoadScopeScheduling._split_scope.

tasks.prompt: Fix open issue #1278 source-faithfully in xdist.dsession.DSession.worker_errordown, the process-down callback used when a worker terminates before sending workerfinished. An unclean direct process exit must retain the established worker-error lifecycle and, after the configured restart limit is exhausted, set a terminal failure signal instead of allowing a green session. Do not treat workerfinished exitstatus 1 as a crash: pytest_sessionfinish sends that event for ordinary failed tests. Preserve keyboard-interrupt, orderly workerfinished, and recoverable restart behavior.
acceptance: An orderly workerfinished event with exitstatus 1 remains a normal completion: it emits exactly one error=None nodedown hook call, removes the worker, and neither shuts down nor restarts it.

A direct process-down error with restarting disabled emits exactly one non-None nodedown diagnostic, removes the dead worker, shuts the session down without a replacement, and sets a terminal failure signal.
Below the restart limit, a process-down error keeps the existing replacement-worker lifecycle and does not set the terminal failure signal.
The production change is confined to src/xdist/dsession.py at xdist.dsession.DSession.worker_errordown, so it composes with the #1219 pytest_sessionstart change.

tasks.prompt: Implement the controller-side worker-startup extension of open issue #1219 in xdist.dsession.DSession.pytest_sessionstart. When the existing parsed --ramp duration is nonzero, invoke the normal pytest_xdist_setupnodes hook once and create workers in declared order, sleeping evenly between starts so the first and last starts span the configured duration. Keep the existing zero-ramp setup_nodes path unchanged; do not duplicate hook notifications or leak workers. Worker-side first-test delay remains in the frozen base.
acceptance: With --ramp=6 and three worker specs, DSession starts worker indices 0, 1, and 2 in order and waits exactly 3 seconds between adjacent starts.
The lifecycle invokes pytest_xdist_setupnodes exactly once before individual starts, preserving the hook that NodeManager.setup_nodes normally emits.
All started nodes are retained as active nodes after session startup.
With a zero ramp, DSession continues through NodeManager.setup_nodes without individual starts, sleeps, or duplicate setup-hook calls.
The production change is contained in src/xdist/dsession.py inside xdist.dsession.DSession and has no live-process evaluator dependency.
